correctness.rationale: The gradient forces W=0, and any projective critical point has XYZ nonzero, giving t³=−27 by multiplication. Conversely at that parameter the partials vanish at [1:1:−3/t:0], with the equation following by Euler's relation. For every smooth parameter the nine stated points have triple tangent contact: on −tρX+3Y+3ρ²Z=0 the branch polynomial restricts to (1+t³/27)X³ by cancellation of the two cross terms and Z³. Smooth plane cubics in this characteristic have nine flexes, and their tangents are distinct by degree. Pullback of each tangent gives the three distinct line graphs W=ηX (with the coordinate permuted at the other flexes), so the 27 lines are exhausted. Since the deck-root parameter is common to the rational flex tangents when q≡1 mod 3, Frobenius is the identity on all line classes in the split case and a common nontrivial deck power in the nonsplit case. For the latter, independently of the tame Lefschetz computation, the invariant H² of the deck action is the H² of the finite quotient P²: the invariant part of the finite pushforward is the constant sheaf (geometric fibers are single group orbits), and averaging is exact over Q_l. Thus the invariant rank is one, with the other six eigenvalues split equally between primitive cube roots by the rational integral Picard action. For q≡2 mod 3 the unique rational cube root and unique rational root of unity give three fixed lines and twelve pairs, all splitting quadratically; the projection is a bijection on base-field points, so the Picard trace is 1 and multiplicities are 4 and 3. The line classes generate Picard, and H² is its Tate twist, with odd cohomology zero and the other even factors 1−T and 1−q²T, giving the stated point counts over every extension. An independent exhaustive RREF scan of 2-planes tests vanishing at four distinct arguments of the binary cubic on each line, and independent normalized projective representative counts reproduce all smooth parameter results over F5, F7, F11 and F13, including both stated frequency examples.
residual_risks: The RREF replay checks four prime fields; the all-extension result uses the symbolic flex restriction and the Picard/cohomological argument. No isomorphism classification and no characteristic-two or -three claim is audited.

originality.rationale: Credit the flex/deck geometry, general finite-field cubic-surface trace and Weyl-class tables, and the Fermat subcase. The supported distinct result is the arithmetic of each marked equation, with a single coefficientwise cube test controlling the line fields and the Picard factor for every allowed field. The closest broader Weyl reconstruction has a different input and does not supply this map. No distinct covering coefficientwise result was established in the inspected materials.
residual_risks: Classical explicit treatments of Hesse/arithmetic cyclic cubic surfaces or uninspected portions of positive-characteristic classification could contain equivalent formulas. The two unnamed Fermat comparisons in the frozen prose were not identified bibliographically beyond checking the named indexed analogues above. No priority conclusion is drawn from same-day dates.

value.rationale: A coefficientwise descent criterion is useful for this natural symmetric pencil: it distinguishes the split and line-free fibers without enumerating lines and supplies point counts over every extension, not only a list of possible Weyl classes. Its nonconstant behavior in small fields makes the parameter dependence substantive. The result is an exact arithmetic refinement of the established flex geometry and an explicit test case for the general cubic-surface Frobenius framework.
residual_risks: Value attaches to the uniform coefficient test and classification, not to recovering the known Fermat specialization in isolation.
